bullets.title: S&P 500 hits new ATH at 7,600; 5 consecutive record closes; 23rd in 2026
bullets.body: The S&P 500 closed at 7,600.71 (+0.27%) on Monday, its 23rd all-time high in 2026 and fifth consecutive record session. The rally was underpinned by AI infrastructure optimism, Iran ceasefire signals, and strong ISM Manufacturing data (5th consecutive month above 50). By pre-market Tuesday, futures were off slightly (SPX -0.15%, NDX -0.05%) with 10-year yields +3bps to 4.43%.

bullets.title: AI capex arms race accelerates: Alphabet raises $80B equity, total hyperscaler spend seen exceeding $700B in 2026
bullets.body: Alphabet announced an $80B equity capital raise ($40B ATM, $15B common, $15B mandatory converts, $10B Berkshire private placement) to fund AI data center buildout, with 2026 capex guided $180-190B. Combined AI capex from Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon is expected to exceed $700B in 2026 with Wall Street projecting above $1T in 2027. Analysts viewed the equity-over-debt choice as a signal that AI data center financing markets are becoming less favorable and may pressure META's more aggressive AGI spending agenda.

bullets.title: Semis surge on AI demand signals: SOXX +2.3%; MRVL +18-21%, HPE +25-28% pre-market
bullets.body: Jensen Huang called Marvell "the next $1T company" at Computex, sparking a 21% pre-market surge (vs current ~$191B market cap). HPE reported Q2 revenue of $10.7B (+40% YoY, vs $9.8B consensus), raised FY26 EPS guide to $3.35-3.45 (vs prior $2.30-2.50), and guided FY27 revenue +8-12% with $4.5B+ FCF. The semiconductor index (SOXX) broadly gained 2.32% as SK Hynix announced plans to double memory wafer capacity over five years and DRAM prices tracked 58-63% Q2 gains.

bullets.title: Software sector reversed: IGV +40%+ off lows, but 51% of software stocks overbought on RSI
bullets.body: Software (IGV) surged 15% over three sessions and 7.9% on Monday as short covering drove a mean-reversion trade from 0th-percentile positioning; security software led (+20.9% YTD). However, Jefferies flagged 51% of software names screening overbought on 14D RSI — highest in ~12 months — and JPM noted the Semis-to-Software positioning gap (Semis at 100th percentile, Software at 0th) is rapidly closing. Retail investors bought a record $46M of IGV on Monday.

bullets.title: Goldman downgrades INTU to Sell (PT $276, 22% downside) on AI-driven tax competition risk
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs cut Intuit to Sell from Neutral with a $276 PT (vs current ~$354), citing AI-driven competition in tax preparation expected to erode market share and ARPU. Goldman's FY28 EPS estimates are 13% below Street consensus. Intuit fell ~5.9% in pre-market as INTU faces incremental negatives including Mailchimp growth deceleration and projected margin compression.

bullets.title: Hedge funds net-buying equities at fastest pace since June 2025; gross leverage near 5-year highs
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs's May positioning report showed hedge funds net-bought global equities for a second consecutive month at the fastest pace since June 2025, led by Info Tech, Financials, and Consumer Discretionary. Gross leverage increased at one of the fastest paces in five years, with overall net leverage at the 84th percentile (5yr). JPM flagged that Tech/Momentum exposure is near historical highs with a key near-term reversal risk.

bullets.title: Oil surged 4-6.5%; Iran-Hormuz risk persists but deal optimism limits upside
bullets.body: Brent crude settled at $94.98/bbl (+4.24%) and WTI at $92.16 (+5.49%) on fears Iran may halt U.S. nuclear negotiations. Trump subsequently stated talks are "continuing at rapid pace" and expects an agreement within a week including Hormuz reopening, causing crude to pull back toward $91-93/bbl by Tuesday morning. Jefferies noted the crisis has shifted from single-chokepoint (Hormuz) to potential dual-chokepoint risk (Bab el-Mandeb), which would extend disruption into global shipping and LNG flows.

bullets.title: Inflation watch: Hedgeye nowcasts May CPI at +4.24% y/y; Wolfe forecasts below-consensus May core CPI
bullets.body: Hedgeye projects May CPI at +4.24% YoY (down 3bps) with June tracking toward +3.95% (-29bps), though Iran War energy disruptions are expected to overwhelm shelter and core services disinflation. Separately, Wolfe Research forecasts May core CPI at 0.24% MoM (below consensus 0.3%), with memory chip price inflation creating a CPI/PCE wedge. Euro area headline CPI rose to 3.2% YoY in May, driven by services inflation jumping 0.5ppt to 3.5%. Rabobank forecasts a 25bp ECB hike in September.

bullets.title: Credit stress signals: consumer loan delinquencies at 9-year high; options bulls at 5-year extreme
bullets.body: U.S. consumer loans 30+ days past due climbed to 4.8% in Q1 2026 (9-year high); credit card serious delinquencies hit 13.1% (highest since Q4 2010, approaching 2008 crisis peak at 13.7%); auto loan delinquencies reached a record 5.6%. Separately, the put/call ratio fell to 0.64 — the most bullish options positioning in 5+ years — while the spread between single-stock vol and S&P 500 index vol is at a record high and the VIX fell to 16.1.

bullets.title: Compute infrastructure buildout: data center construction hits $50B+ in April; ISM Manufacturing at 3-year high
bullets.body: U.S. data center construction spending eclipsed $50B in April for the first time ever. ISM Manufacturing showed five consecutive months above 50 — its strongest streak in 3+ years — with upside in New Orders, Backlog, and New Export Orders. JPM upgraded its Q2 2026 GDP forecast from 2.0% to 2.5%, with NFP expectations at 75k (vs 85k Street), implying ~1.0% SPX move on the print.

bullets.title: EU trade deal advancing: Parliament trade committee votes to remove US duties ahead of July 4 deadline
bullets.body: The EU Parliament's trade committee voted to remove duties on many U.S. goods ahead of Trump's July 4 compliance deadline, and EU lawmakers subsequently cleared the deal for final approval. This is a macro positive for US equities and reduces transatlantic trade risk premium.

bullets.title: Memory super-cycle continues: HDD supply shortage through 2028; DRAM +58-63% Q2; SK Hynix doubling capacity
bullets.body: Citi raised estimates and PTs on STX and WDC citing AI-driven HDD exabyte demand growing ~25% CAGR, with current supply shortfall of hundreds of EBs expected to persist through 2028. HDD makers are focusing on areal density gains rather than new unit capacity. TrendForce projects DRAM contract prices up 58-63% in Q2 following Q1's 93-98% surge, with inventory at extreme lows.

bullets.title: NVDA Computex keynotes: Vera CPU demand to exceed GPU lineup; 50%+ FCF return commitment
bullets.body: Jensen Huang at GTC Taipei stated demand for the Vera CPU is likely to exceed Nvidia's GPU lineup — framing it as a "major growth driver" for a $200B market. Nvidia committed to returning 50%+ of FCF to shareholders in 2026. The company confirmed adequate supply for robust CPU and GPU growth while acknowledging some constraints, and reaffirmed export compliance and commitment to China and Taiwan supply chains.

bullets.title: Anthropic files confidential S-1; Polymarket gives 78% odds it IPOs before OpenAI
bullets.body: Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft S-1 registration statement with the SEC following its $65B fundraise at a $900B-965B post-money valuation. Polymarket shows 78% odds Anthropic IPOs before OpenAI. Salesforce's stake in Anthropic now totals ~$5B; Palo Alto Networks used Anthropic's Mythos to identify critical vulnerabilities. OpenAI's Altman stated he is not focused on IPO timing.

bullets.title: Global bond yields declining: JGB 10Y -10bps to 2.58%; Germany Bund -5bps; gold replaced Treasuries as top reserve asset
bullets.body: Japan's 10-year JGB yield fell 10bps to 2.58% ahead of a strong auction, with the 40-year down 7bps to 3.745%; Germany's Bund fell 5bps to 2.963%; Italy's 10Y -6.5bps to 3.69%. The ECB reported that gold has surpassed U.S. Treasuries as the world's top reserve asset. SMFG called on the BOJ to present a clear normalization path and raise rates in June, while the BOJ stated readiness for emergency bond-buying if markets destabilize.

bullets.title: IBM invests $10B+ in quantum computing; QBTS analyst day drives PT raise to $40
bullets.body: IBM announced plans to invest more than $10B in quantum computing over five years, targeting the world's first large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029. Roth raised D-Wave Quantum (QBTS) PT to $40 from $30 after the company's first investor analyst day, citing dual gate/annealing positioning, a recent $10M enterprise QCaaS win, and at least two hardware deals expected in CY26.

bullets.title: Short-seller Andrew Left convicted of securities fraud in Los Angeles federal court
bullets.body: Citron Research founder Andrew Left was found guilty of securities fraud by a federal jury in Los Angeles for publicly posting recommendations that contradicted his actual trading positions. The conviction has broader market implications for social-media-driven equity commentary and disclosure standards.

bullets.title: Broad market breadth remains narrow: >50% of S&P 500 constituents trade below 100-day MA
bullets.body: Despite the S&P 500 hitting new all-time highs, more than half of S&P 500 constituent stocks trade below their 100-day moving average, and Monday's 8-session ATH streak was notable for having more decliners than advancers—the longest such streak on record per JPM. Sector breadth was narrow with only Tech and Energy in the green on Monday.

bullets.title: GOOGL $80B raise framed as financing-conditions inflection, not dilution signal
bullets.body: Opco and Jefferies highlighted that Alphabet's decision to use equity rather than credit for its $80B AI capex raise — the most notable US equity financing for a company with market cap >$500B since Tesla in 2020 — signals that data center financing via credit is becoming less favorable. Analysts flagged this should create greater pressure on Meta and other hyperscalers to demonstrate ROI discipline. Google held $126B in cash and marketable securities at March 31, and generated $174B in operating cash flow over the past 12 months.
